dimension: The GROUP surface — member/officer dashboard (app/(dashboard)/**, excluding admin)
summary: The group surface is functionally complete and its SQL is well-written — no N+1 loops, no missing tenant filters, and the two heaviest aggregate endpoints (executive summary, risk) are Redis-cached. Its cost is almost entirely *structural*, not data-driven: with 37 group_members, 23 contributions and 66 journal_lines in production, every read executes in under 3ms, yet a single /accounting page view issues ~57 database round trips and a /dashboard view ~60, because nine accounting reports fire regardless of which of eight tabs is visible and because `withDb()` spends five round trips on BEGIN/three set_config/COMMIT before every statement. EXPLAIN ANALYZE on live prod shows query *planning* costs 8–25× execution (13.4ms cold / 2.27ms warm planning vs 0.45 / 0.27ms execution, 802 shared buffers touched during planning alone) — the group surface is where the schema's 1,253 indexes and 278 policies are actually paid for. The degradation order as groups grow is: /accounting first (four unbounded full-year ledger aggregates per view, none cached), then /dashboard, then /members/[id]; and two screens will break functionally before they get slow — a `pageSize` param the members API has never accepted silently caps the loan and welfare member pickers at 20 people.

findings.title: /accounting fires all 9 report queries on every view regardless of which of 8 tabs is open — ~57 DB round trips for one tab
findings.evidence: app/(dashboard)/accounting/page.tsx:52-72 declares useAccounts, useTrialBalance, useJournals, useProfitAndLoss, useBalanceSheet, useCashFlow, useEquityChanges, useFiscalPeriods, useApprovalPolicies at the top level of AccountingPage. Only useProfitAndLoss/useCashFlow/useEquityChanges carry `enabled`, and it is `!!(from && to)` where from/to are unconditionally-computed strings (page.tsx:49-50), so it is always true. The active tab is local state (page.tsx:36) that gates nothing. Statement counts: accounts 1 (accounting.service.ts:250), trial_balance 1 (:398), journals 2 (app/api/v1/accounting/journals/route.ts:26,30), P&L 1 (:423), balance_sheet 1 (:484), cash_flow 2 (:542,:568), equity_changes 2 (:623,:643), fiscal-periods 1 (fiscal-periods.service.ts:29), policies 1 = 12 SQL statements across 9 withDb calls = 12 + 9×5 transaction-control statements = 57 round trips. None of these paths call `cached()` — grep of `cached(` across lib/services shows it used only by admin.service, analytics.service and organization-finance.service, never by accounting.service. The correct pattern already exists two files over: app/(dashboard)/treasury/page.tsx:213-215 uses `enabled: tab === 'reversals'` etc., and app/(dashboard)/reports/page.tsx:21-27 uses `enabled: false` with manual refetch.
findings.impact: Highest DB work per view on the entire group surface. 8 of the 12 statements produce data the user cannot see. P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and equity are unbounded full-year aggregates over journal_lines×journal_entries×accounts — they cost ~0.5ms each at 66 journal_lines but scale linearly with a group's posting volume forever, since none is cached and every one recomputes Jan-1-to-Dec-31 from scratch. This is the screen that degrades first.
findings.recommendation: Add `enabled: tab === '<name>'` to the seven tab-scoped hooks (leave accounts + trial balance, the default tab). That alone drops a first paint from 9 HTTP calls / 57 round trips to 2 / 11. Separately, wrap getTrialBalance/getProfitAndLoss/getBalanceSheet/getCashFlowStatement/getEquityChanges in the existing `cached(keys.cache(...), 60, ...)` helper, keyed by groupId plus the date arguments — the same 60s TTL analytics.service.ts:119 already uses.

findings.title: withDb() spends 5 network round trips of pure transaction/context overhead before every statement — 3 separate set_config calls that collapse into 1
findings.evidence: lib/db/index.ts:121-131 `setTenantLocals` issues three sequentially-awaited statements: `SELECT set_config($1,$2,TRUE)` for app.current_user_id, app.current_group_id and app.current_role (plus a fourth for organizationId). lib/db/index.ts:141-153 wraps them in an explicit `BEGIN` and `COMMIT`. So every withDb() call = BEGIN + 3 set_config + <work> + COMMIT = 5 statements carrying no data. Live prod pg_stat_statements confirms the volume: `SELECT set_config($1, $2, $3)` 6,591 calls / 346ms total exec, plus a second normalized form at 6,409 calls / 454ms — server-side execution is 0.05-0.07ms each, i.e. the entire cost is network latency, not Postgres. Every one of the 12 group screens pays this per API call: /accounting 9×5=45 overhead statements, /dashboard 10×5=50, /members/[id] 5×5=25, /welfare 3×5=15. The Supabase project is in eu-central-1 (get_project: region eu-central-1); vercel.json contains only `{"buildCommand": "npm run build"}` with no `regions` key, so functions run in the project's default region — I could not verify which (list_teams returns empty for this personal account), so the per-RTT figure is unverified, but the round-trip *count* is deterministic from the code.
findings.impact: Two thirds of the group surface's database round trips carry zero data. At a conservative 5ms intra-region RTT that is ~225ms of pure overhead on an /accounting load; if functions and DB are on different continents (a real risk given eu-central-1 and an unset region) it is several seconds. The three set_config calls are trivially mergeable — they are independent and already parameterised.
findings.recommendation: Replace the three awaits in setTenantLocals with one statement: `SELECT set_config($1,$2,TRUE), set_config($3,$4,TRUE), set_config($5,$6,TRUE)` (append a fourth pair when organizationId is present). That removes 2 round trips from every DB-touching request on the platform — ~24 per /accounting view. Separately, confirm the Vercel function region and pin it to `fra1` in vercel.json to match eu-central-1; that single line is worth more than every query optimisation on this list if the regions currently differ.

findings.title: Loan and welfare member pickers silently show only 20 members — `pageSize: 200` is a param the members API has never accepted, and the fix is already documented in the same repo
findings.evidence: app/(dashboard)/loans/page.tsx:52 `useMembers({ pageSize: 200 })` and app/(dashboard)/welfare/page.tsx:68 `useMembers({ pageSize: 200 })`. lib/validators/member.schema.ts:63 defines `limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(20)` — there is no `pageSize` key, and the route parses with `MemberQuerySchema.parse(Object.fromEntries(searchParams))` (app/api/v1/members/route.ts:11), so zod's default strip-unknown-keys drops `pageSize` and `limit` falls to 20. The rosters feed the member `<select>` inside the apply-loan dialog (loans/page.tsx:154) and the welfare-request dialog (welfare/page.tsx:307). The same bug class was already found and fixed twice in this repo: app/(dashboard)/contributions/page.tsx:46-47 carries the comment "`limit` (not `pageSize`) is the param the members API reads; its max is 100", and lib/validators/sms.schema.ts:64 documents "`ComposeTab` used to try, asking for a non-existent `pageSize: 500` that Zod silently stripped — so 'Send to All Members' reached the default 20 and no error was raised anywhere." Not yet visible in prod: the largest group is CAPITAL POINT CHAMA at 9 members (SELECT g.name, count(gm.id) FROM groups g LEFT JOIN group_members gm ...).
findings.impact: Any group with more than 20 members cannot select members 21+ when applying for a loan or filing a welfare request — the two highest-value write flows on the surface — with no error shown anywhere. It also caps at 100 even once corrected, so the roster needs a real answer above 100. Secondarily both hooks fetch eagerly on page load for a dialog that is closed by default, so the cost is paid by every visitor who never opens it.
findings.recommendation: Change both to `useMembers({ limit: 100, status: 'active' })`, matching contributions/page.tsx:52 exactly. Gate both on dialog state (`{ enabled: open }`) so the roster is not fetched for visitors who never open the dialog. For groups above 100 members, follow the precedent sms.schema.ts:64 established — resolve the audience server-side rather than paging the client through /members.

findings.title: Query planning costs 8–25× execution on the group surface — 802 shared buffers touched per plan, and node-pg re-plans every statement
findings.evidence: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) run on live prod against the exact members-list SQL from lib/services/members.service.ts:153. Cold: `Planning: Buffers: shared hit=801 read=1 / Planning Time: 13.396 ms / Execution Time: 0.451 ms`. Warm re-run: `Buffers: shared hit=802 / Planning Time: 2.265 ms / Execution Time: 0.271 ms`. Trial balance (accounting.service.ts:398): `Planning Time: 5.608 ms / Execution Time: 0.547 ms`, 655 planning buffers. Catalog size: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_class WHERE relkind='i' = 1,253 indexes, relkind='r' = 255 tables, pg_policy = 278 policies. Empty tables still carrying full index sets, verified by row count + pg_index: meeting_attendance 8 indexes / 0 rows, meeting_resolutions 7 / 0, share_transactions 12 / 0, member_investment_shares 5 / 0, investment_returns 5 / 0, investment_expenses 4 / 0 — ~41 indexes on 6 permanently-empty tables, all of them on the group surface's own hot path. node-pg's `client.query(sql, params)` uses unnamed extended-protocol statements (no `name` field anywhere in the codebase), so no plan is cached and this is paid per statement, per request.
findings.impact: Extends the lead's already-banked '481 of 800 indexes have idx_scan=0' finding into a measured user-facing cost: on the group surface, Postgres spends 8–25× longer choosing a plan than running it. At ~2.3ms warm planning × the 12 statements of an /accounting view, planning alone is ~28ms of the request, against ~4ms of actual execution. This is the mechanism by which schema bloat bills the highest-traffic path.
findings.recommendation: Drop the ~41 indexes on the six zero-row tables first — they are the cheapest to prove safe (no rows, no scans that matter) and they sit directly on group-surface queries. Then work through the lead's 481-index idx_scan=0 list. Re-run the two EXPLAINs above afterwards as the acceptance test: planning buffers should fall well below 800.

findings.title: /welfare/pool runs 4 SQL statements and 2 of them feed a field no client has ever read — paid on both /dashboard and /welfare
findings.evidence: app/api/v1/welfare/pool/route.ts:13-17 `Promise.all([welfareService.getPoolSummary(ctx), welfareService.listPoolContributions(ctx, {page, limit})])` returning `{ summary, contributions }`. getPoolSummary is 2 statements (welfare.service.ts:206, :213); listPoolContributions is 2 more (welfare.service.ts:266 items, :275 a COUNT(*)). Every consumer reads only `.summary`: app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:193 `poolData?.summary?.balance`, app/(dashboard)/welfare/page.tsx:148 `poolData?.summary`. The redundancy is already known and written down — hooks/use-welfare.ts:37-38 types the field as `contributions: unknown` with the comment "Not modeled precisely — not consumed client-side today (no page_size in the real response)."
findings.impact: Half the statements on this endpoint are waste, and it is called on two screens including the dashboard — the highest-traffic path. The unused COUNT(*) over welfare_pool_contributions is an unbounded aggregate that grows with every pool contribution ever recorded.
findings.recommendation: Return `contributions` only when the caller asks for it (e.g. `?include=contributions`), or drop it from the GET entirely and give the pool ledger its own route. Then delete the dead `contributions: unknown` field from WelfarePoolResponse.

findings.title: Member profile's "Total Contributed" and "Active Loans" are JS reductions over a 10-row page, presented as lifetime totals
findings.evidence: app/(dashboard)/members/[id]/page.tsx:84 `useContributions({ memberId: id, limit: 10 })` and :85 `useLoans({ memberId: id, limit: 10 })`. Line 127-128: `const totalContributed = contributions.reduce((sum, c) => sum + parseFloat(c.amount ?? '0'), 0)` where `contributions = contribData?.items ?? []` (:125). Line 199 renders it as `<StatCard title="Total Contributed" value={formatKES(totalContributed)} />`. Line 202 does the same for `Active Loans` — `loans.filter(l => l.status === 'active' || l.status === 'disbursed').length` over the 10-row loan page. Both `memberId` and `limit` ARE honoured by the server (lib/validators/contribution.schema.ts:27, loan.schema.ts:104), so the slice is real, not a stripped-param accident. Not yet wrong in prod: `SELECT count(*) FROM contributions c WHERE (SELECT count(*) FROM contributions c2 WHERE c2.member_id=c.member_id)>10` returns 0 — no member has passed 10 contributions yet.
findings.impact: A latent wrong number on every member profile that fires the moment any member records an 11th contribution — roughly one year of monthly saving. It understates silently, with no truncation indicator, on the single number a member most cares about. Also the wrong shape of work: a SUM the database can do in one aggregate is being done by shipping rows to the browser.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-member totals endpoint (or extend GET /members/:id) returning SUM(amount) and the active-loan count computed in SQL, and render the 10-row lists purely as "recent activity". member-balances.service.ts already exists and may already hold the right query.

findings.title: Every paginated list endpoint runs its COUNT and its page sequentially — the Promise.all fix already exists in shares.service.ts
findings.evidence: Sequential awaits, count first then page: lib/services/members.service.ts:144 then :153; contributions.service.ts:29 then :34; loans.service.ts:29 then :34; investments.service.ts:80 then :98; welfare.service.ts:266 then :275; meetings.service.ts:102 then :116; app/api/v1/accounting/journals/route.ts:26 then :30. The two queries are fully independent — neither consumes the other's result. lib/services/shares.service.ts:426-429 (`const [{rows: cnt}, {rows: items}] = await Promise.all([...])`) and :563-565 already do it correctly, so the pattern is established in-repo. Live cost, pg_stat_statements: the members COUNT (`SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM group_members gm JOIN members m ...`) 204 calls at mean 2.140ms, and the members page query 204 calls at mean 1.518ms — serialised into 3.66ms of DB time where 2.14ms would do, plus a whole extra network round trip.
findings.impact: One avoidable round trip on every list view across 7 screens — /members, /contributions, /loans, /meetings, /investments, /welfare, /accounting journals. At scale the COUNT is also the query that degrades first, since it cannot use the LIMIT to stop early.
findings.recommendation: Replace each sequential pair with `Promise.all`, copying shares.service.ts:426-429 verbatim. Seven mechanical edits, no behaviour change.

findings.title: The dashboard runs a 15-query executive summary to display three numbers
findings.evidence: app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:138-145 fetches `/analytics/executive?period=12mo` and consumes exactly three fields at :207-213 — `contributions.totalAmount`, `loans.outstandingBalance`, `contributions.monthlyBuckets.at(-1)?.amount`. That endpoint is lib/services/analytics.service.ts:116, whose `Promise.all` at :141-345 issues 15 aggregate queries across group_members, contributions (×3), loans (×4), welfare (×2), shares (×2), dividends (×2) and credit_scores. Mitigated but not eliminated by `cached(keys.cache('executive-summary', groupId:period), 60, ...)` at analytics.service.ts:119 — real Upstash Redis (lib/redis/index.ts:196), so the cache is shared across Lambda instances and the 15 queries run at most once per group per minute.
findings.impact: On a cache miss the dashboard pays 15 aggregate queries plus a withDb transaction for three scalars — every one of those aggregates grows with the group's history and none of the other 12 results is rendered anywhere on this page. It also means the dashboard's slowest query is one built for a different screen.
findings.recommendation: Either add a `?fields=` projection to /analytics/executive so the dashboard requests only the contributions and loans blocks, or give the dashboard a small dedicated endpoint with three SUMs. The 60s cache makes this lower priority than #1 and #2 — do it after those.

findings.title: Five React Query cache keys for one member roster, and three shared endpoints fetched twice under different keys across screens
findings.evidence: Same URL, different keys — zero cache reuse when navigating between screens. (1) `/analytics/executive?period=12mo`: dashboard/page.tsx:142 `['dashboard','executive-summary']` vs analytics/page.tsx:76 `['analytics','executive',period]`. (2) `/accounting/reports?type=trial_balance`: dashboard/page.tsx:129 `['dashboard','trial-balance']` vs hooks/use-accounting.ts:8,25 `['accounting','trial-balance']` (used by accounting/page.tsx:53). (3) `/mpesa/unrouted`: dashboard/page.tsx:115 `['dashboard','mpesa-unrouted']` vs mpesa/unrouted/page.tsx:46 `['mpesa','unrouted']`. (4) The member roster is requested five ways: contributions/page.tsx:52 `{limit:100,status:'active'}`, loans/page.tsx:52 `{pageSize:200}`, welfare/page.tsx:68 `{pageSize:200}`, mpesa/unrouted/page.tsx:50 `['mpesa','unrouted','members']` → `/members?status=active&limit=200`, mpesa/reallocations/page.tsx:79 `['mpesa','reallocations','members']` → the identical URL under a different key. The counter-example proving the codebase can do this right: members/[id]/page.tsx:95 and credit-scores/[memberId]/page.tsx:84 both use `['credit-score', id, 'latest']` for `/credit-scores/:id` and share the cache correctly.
findings.impact: Navigating dashboard → accounting refetches the trial balance; dashboard → analytics refetches the 15-query executive summary; dashboard → /mpesa/unrouted refetches the unrouted list. The roster — the single most reused dataset on the surface — is fetched from scratch on each of five screens, and two of those five (items 4a/4b) hit byte-identical URLs.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one shared roster hook (e.g. `useActiveMemberRoster()` with a fixed key and a long staleTime) and use it on all five screens. Replace the three ad-hoc `['dashboard', ...]` keys with the canonical hooks — `useTrialBalance()` from use-accounting.ts already exists and the dashboard should just call it. Establish the rule that the query key is derived from the URL, not from the screen.

findings.title: investments.service.getById runs 4 sequential queries, one against a table that provably cannot return rows, then the page re-derives totals SQL already computed
findings.evidence: lib/services/investments.service.ts:105-141: query 1 the investment (:108), then three sequentially-awaited unbounded child queries — returns (:120), expenses (:127), member_investment_shares (:134) — none with a LIMIT, none dependent on the others. The fourth is guaranteed empty: `SELECT count(*) FROM member_investment_shares` = 0 on prod, and hooks/use-investments.ts:59-63 documents why — "member_investment_shares has no writer anywhere in the product, so this is always empty today." The table nonetheless carries 5 indexes. Then app/(dashboard)/investments/[id]/page.tsx:186-189 computes `totalReturns`/`totalExpenses` with `.reduce()` over those unbounded lists, even though the list endpoint already returns SQL-computed `total_returns` and `total_expenses` (typed at hooks/use-investments.ts:27,29, computed in investments.service.ts:80).
findings.impact: Four sequential round trips where one plus a parallel batch of two would do, one of them a query with a provably empty result set on every single investment detail view. The JS reduction also means the detail page's totals and the list page's totals are computed by two different code paths, which is how they drift.
findings.recommendation: Wrap returns + expenses in `Promise.all`. Delete the shares query and its UI section until member_investment_shares has a writer (drop its 5 indexes with it). Read `inv.total_returns` / `inv.total_expenses` on the detail page instead of reducing.

findings.title: GET /accounting/journals accepts an unbounded, unvalidated `limit` — the only list endpoint on the surface without a zod cap
findings.evidence: app/api/v1/accounting/journals/route.ts:13-14: `const page = parseInt(searchParams.get('page') ?? '1', 10); const limit = parseInt(searchParams.get('limit') ?? '20', 10);` — no schema, no `.max()`, no NaN guard, then fed straight into `LIMIT $n OFFSET $n+1` at :43. Every peer endpoint uses a zod schema with an explicit ceiling: member.schema.ts:63 max(100), contribution.schema.ts:26 max(100), loan.schema.ts:104 max(100), dividends.schema.ts:53 max(100), shares.schema.ts:93 max(200), credit-scores.schema.ts:11 max(200), whatsapp.schema.ts:31 max(200).
findings.impact: `?limit=1000000` from any authenticated group member returns every journal entry the group has ever posted, each with a `COUNT(jl.id)` GROUP BY — the heaviest read on the accounting surface, with no ceiling. `?limit=abc` produces `LIMIT NaN` and a 500. On the general ledger this is the table that grows fastest.
findings.recommendation: Add a `JournalQuerySchema` to lib/validators/accounting.schema.ts with `page`/`limit` matching the max(100) convention and parse with it, exactly as app/api/v1/members/route.ts:11 does.

findings.title: The dashboard blocks its entire render on the slowest of ten independent queries
findings.evidence: app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:161-173 builds `dashboardQueries` from all ten hooks and sets `isDashboardLoading = dashboardQueries.some(q => q.isLoading)`. Lines 225-236 return a full-page skeleton while that is true. The ten include the 15-query executive summary (:138), the trial balance (:128), and the unbounded non-contributors scan (:121). The permission gating itself is free — lib/auth/use-permission.ts:23-28 reads useAuth() state with no fetch, and the four gated queries carry `enabled: canView*` so they never enter the loading set — but every ungated query does.
findings.impact: Time-to-first-content on the highest-traffic screen equals max(all ten API latencies), not the fastest. One slow endpoint blanks the whole page; the 'Needs you now' task list and the member count cannot paint until the executive summary and trial balance both land.
findings.recommendation: Drop the page-level gate and let each card own its own skeleton — the Skeleton component is already imported (:13) and StatCard/TaskRow are independent. The existing comment at :153-160 acknowledges the tradeoff was taken 'pragmatically'; the cheap version is to keep the aggregate error banner and remove only the aggregate loading gate.

findings.title: members.service.list ships all 30 columns including password_hash and reset_otp_hash, then strips them in JavaScript
findings.evidence: lib/services/members.service.ts:153-162 selects `m.*` from members. `SELECT count(*), string_agg(column_name,...) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='members'` returns 30 columns including password_hash, reset_otp_hash, reset_otp_expires_at, reset_otp_attempts, session_version. They are removed after the fact at :164 via `stripSecrets(applyMemberMask(...))`. Same pattern at :172 (getById) and in accounting.service.ts:252 (`SELECT * FROM accounts`).
findings.impact: Password and OTP hashes cross the network on every member-list page load before being discarded — a wide-row read that is also a security smell, and one refactor away from leaking if a future caller forgets stripSecrets. Widens every row on the surface's most-fetched list.
findings.recommendation: Replace `m.*` with the explicit projection the SafeMember type already describes. The type is the spec; the query should match it rather than being corrected afterwards in JS.

findings.title: contributions.nonContributors returns the full unbounded set to render five names and a count
findings.evidence: lib/services/contributions.service.ts:53-72 runs an unbounded `SELECT m.id, name FROM group_members gm JOIN members m ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (completed contribution this month) ORDER BY m.first_name` with no LIMIT, then `return { count: rows.length, sample: rows.slice(0, 5) }` at :70. The consumer is app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx:121-126, which renders `nonContrib.count` and `nonContrib.sample` (capped again to 3 by TaskRow's `preview.slice(0, 3)` at :80). The code comment at :49-51 acknowledges it: "small per group, so we return the full set and let the caller cap the preview."
findings.impact: Early in a calendar month almost nobody has contributed, so this returns nearly the whole roster to display three names. Bounded by group size, so it degrades linearly with the thing the product is trying to grow.
findings.recommendation: Return the count and a LIMIT 5 sample in one query — `SELECT count(*) OVER () AS total, ... LIMIT 5` — rather than materialising the full set.

findings.title: The meetings list has no index for its default sort and fiscal_periods has no LIMIT at all
findings.evidence: EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) of meetings.service.ts:102 with no status filter, run on prod, returns `Sort (Sort Key: m.scheduled_at DESC) -> Hash Join -> Seq Scan on meetings (Filter: group_id = ...)`. The two candidate indexes both miss: `idx_meetings_group_status_scheduled (group_id, status, scheduled_at)` cannot serve an unfiltered query because status is the second key column, and `idx_meetings_group_created (group_id, created_at DESC)` sorts the wrong column. (The two correlated per-row subqueries at :106-107 are fine — the plan shows Index Only Scans on idx_attendance_meeting_status and idx_resolutions_meeting_order.) Separately, lib/services/fiscal-periods.service.ts:29-32 is `SELECT * FROM fiscal_periods WHERE group_id = $1 ORDER BY period_start DESC` with no LIMIT, consumed by the always-on useFiscalPeriods on accounting/page.tsx:63.
findings.impact: Every /meetings page load sorts the group's entire meeting history to return 20 rows — a group holding weekly meetings for five years sorts 260 rows per page view, per pagination click. fiscal_periods grows by 12 rows a year per group and is fetched unbounded on every accounting view.
findings.recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX idx_meetings_group_scheduled ON meetings (group_id, scheduled_at DESC)` and drop the redundant `idx_meetings_group_created` and bare `idx_meetings_group` while you are there. Add a LIMIT (or pagination) to fiscal-periods.service.ts:29. Both are cheap; neither is urgent at 2 meetings and 0 fiscal periods.
